question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping maintains firm control over the Chinese Communist Party through extensive elite purges, military reshuffles favoring loyalists, and institutional reforms that eliminated term limits and centralized authority. With the 21st Party Congress scheduled for late 2027 widely expected to grant him a fourth term as general secretary, analysts see no credible internal challengers or succession signals that would force his exit before the end of 2026. Persistent overseas rumors of health concerns, factional pushback, or loss of military support have repeatedly failed to materialize into verifiable developments. Trader consensus at 95 percent for "No" reflects this entrenched position and the absence of scheduled events capable of triggering removal. Only an unforeseen major shock, such as a sudden incapacitating health event or acute crisis eroding elite confidence, could realistically alter the outcome within the resolution window.

eventMetadata.context_description: The 2028 Democratic presidential nomination market reflects a fragmented field with no dominant frontrunner more than two years before primaries begin. Trader consensus clusters Gavin Newsom, Jon Ossoff, and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez at the top, each in the mid-teens, amid broad support for governors, senators, and House members. Newsom’s position stems from his California executive record and early fundraising, while Ossoff and Ocasio-Cortez have gained ground through national visibility and appeal to different party factions. Kamala Harris and Pete Buttigieg trail as former national figures, with the long tail of other names underscoring uncertainty over who will consolidate support. The tight spread aligns with early-cycle dynamics where polling averages remain scattered, 2026 contests may test candidate organizations, and no major endorsements or formal announcements have yet reordered the field. Developments such as midterm outcomes, Senate vote records, or shifts in party messaging on key issues like the economy and foreign policy could widen gaps ahead of 2027–2028.

Trader consensus clusters Gavin Newsom, Jon Ossoff, and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez at the top, each in the mid-teens, amid broad support for governors, senators, and House members. Newsom’s position stems from his California executive record and early fundraising, while Ossoff and Ocasio-Cortez have gained ground through national visibility and appeal to different party factions. Kamala Harris and Pete Buttigieg trail as former national figures, with the long tail of other names underscoring uncertainty over who will consolidate support. The tight spread aligns with early-cycle dynamics where polling averages remain scattered, 2026 contests may test candidate organizations, and no major endorsements or formal announcements have yet reordered the field. Developments such as midterm outcomes, Senate vote records, or shifts in party messaging on key issues like the economy and foreign policy could widen gaps ahead of 2027–2028.
